title: per-block FP8 MMQ prefill kernel, v2 — executing the v1 lane's own recipe
question: v1 delivered kernel-level bit-exactness and measured 0.81-0.94x the Q8_0 MMQ floor at every 27B projection shape, m, and tile in its sweep. Its own verdict named the mechanism (nobody is MMA-bound — both arms sit at 105-127 TF against the .kind::f8f6f4 381-TF class; the floor wins by deferring ALL scaling to one epilogue fold, while v1 paid mixed f32 scale work every 256-k iteration at 1 CTA/SM on a 61 KB tile) and prescribed three changes. This lane implemented all three and measured each.
verdict: EXACTNESS: DELIVERED AGAIN, and model-level quality improved ~130x (perplexity drift +0.11% -> +0.0008%). PERFORMANCE: the recipe worked structurally — v2 goes from uniformly-below-floor to AT OR ABOVE the floor on the wide/long-context shapes (27B m=6257 geomean ~1.00x with 4 of 6 shapes >= 0.99x and q/square above; 1.7B m=6257 1.000-1.064x on 4 of 5) — but it does NOT clear the ~1.1x bar, and local end-to-end pp on the 1.7B is 0.9899x (pp512) / 0.9951x (pp6257). Recipe items 2 and 3 (occupancy, cp.async) are REFUTED with receipts; the entire gain came from item 1 plus the one geometry re-test item 1 licensed. Stays behind MEMRA_FP8_MMQ=1, default OFF.

section: 1. WHAT THE RECIPE'S THREE ITEMS ACTUALLY DID
item1_restructure: POSITIVE and the whole win. Scale block (128) becomes the OUTER k loop; the four k32 MMAs of a block chain into ONE unscaled f32 accumulator; (s_blk*dB) folds once per block. MMQ_ITER_K 256->128, x tile row 64->32 value-ints, smem 61KB->37KB. Lifted every shape 2-6pp with zero exactness loss (commit 82cbe769). Requires the activation scale to be per-128 rather than per-32 — declared, not smuggled: it is an arithmetic change, the host reference in fp8_mmq_check.rs was rewritten to the new grouping, and the EXACT arm re-proves bit-identity against THAT reference.
item2_occupancy: NEGATIVE, both forms (commit 8e94dc61). Y=64 + 4 warps + minBlocks=2 helps ONLY the 5120->1024 shape (1.227x, pure grid-fill on a shape with 16 row tiles) and is 0.7-1.7pp worse on every real shape. Y=128 + OCC=2 is 4-6pp worse everywhere: the 128x128 tile carries 64 floats of accumulator per thread, so demanding 2 blocks/SM caps registers below what the mainloop needs and it spills. MECHANISM the v1 recipe got wrong: halving Y does not raise warps/SM at all — it splits the same 8 warps into two CTAs — so it buys grid parallelism, not latency hiding, and 'latency-exposed at 1 CTA/SM' does not convert into throughput here.
item3_cp_async: NEGATIVE (commit 46d0ce1d, implemented and kept behind FP8_MMQ_PIPE=0). 3-6pp worse than item 1 on every shape. Mechanism: the ACTIVATION tile load is still a synchronous global->smem copy through the register file (18 KB per iteration at X=128, the same order as the 16 KB weight tile) and it sits between the cp.async issue and the wait, so the pipeline removes no stall while adding a wait_group and 18 KB of smem pressure. Experiment B tested that note instead of believing it — X=256 doubles the MMA work per weight copy, the condition under which overlap should start to pay — and CONFIRMED it: the y tile doubles to 36 KB just as fast, and the second weight buffer (91 KB total) costs occupancy outright, 5-10pp below PIPE=0 at the same geometry.

section: 2. WHERE THE GAIN CAME FROM (not from items 2-3)
experiment_A: X=256 on the halved tile (commit 79c7379d). v1's sweep had found X=256 best on its two largest shapes but it needed 61+ KB at MMQ_ITER_K=256 and ran 1 CTA/SM; item 1's halving made it affordable. This was the FIRST time the kernel family exceeded the floor: 27B m=6257 4 of 6 shapes >= 1.0x, m=512 down_proj 1.084x.
selection_bug: the default that shipped experiment A used an out_f-only fallback rule (out_f < 2048 -> X=128), calibrated on 27B shapes. The local pp battery exposed it: on the 1.7B (out_f 1024-6144) it mis-picked X=256 for 4 of 5 projections, 0.535-0.865x floor against X=128's 0.847-0.890x, and pp512 read 0.9808x. Fixed (commit 5b9e8d21) by computing wave fill for both candidates — fill = ctas/(waves*nsm), take wide unless below 86% of narrow — with nsm cached per device. pp512 0.9808 -> 0.9899x. LESSON, and it is the v1 lane's law 2 repeating: a threshold calibrated on one model's shapes is stale the moment the shapes move, and only the second model's own GEMM sheet could show it.

section: 3. PERFORMANCE — GEMM-only vs the Q8_0 MMQ floor
protocol: per shape: warmup both arms, then reps x (fp8blk timed, q8_0 timed) INTERLEAVED inside the rep loop so both share one clock/thermal regime; median of reps (9 at m=512, 5 at m=6257); flock'd. Both arms consume the SAME logical weight: the e4m3 codes are the source and the Q8_0 slab is produced from them by the merged ARM B' device dequant, i.e. the actual floor path. Denominator re-measured in every session; no cross-day denominators.
result: the slice-1 target (>= 1.0x floor) is MET on the shapes that dominate long-context prefill and MISSED on narrow-out_f and on every 1.7B shape at m=512. The ~1.1x bar is not met at any aggregate. down_proj 17408->5120 at m=512 is the single best cell at 1.089x.
why_the_ceiling_is_where_it_is: unchanged from v1's mechanism finding, and v2 is the test of it: both arms still land at 110-130 TF against the 381-TF f8f6f4 class, so the MMA is still not the bottleneck, and e4m3's byte advantage over Q8_0 is only 1.0 vs 1.0625 B/weight = 6%. Item 1 removed the per-iteration f32 scale work that v1 identified as the remaining gap, and the result is parity-class, not a 20% win — which says the residual difference was never the scale fold alone. What is left is the f32 accumulator itself against the floor's s32, and that is structural to per-block FP8 as formulated, not a tuning miss.

section: 4. PERFORMANCE — end-to-end pp on the local rig
pp512: floor 2282.0 tok/s, mmq 2258.9 = 0.9899x (N=5 process reps x 3 in-process, interleaved, flock'd, temp 54-64C)
reconciliation: consistent with the GEMM sheet and bounded by it. At m=512 every 1.7B projection is 0.846-0.894x GEMM-only, yet pp512 is 0.9899x, because attention/norms/rope/lm_head are arm-independent and dilute a ~13% GEMM deficit to ~1%. The 1.7B never reaches the m=6257 cells where this arm wins (1.000-1.064x), because the engine's prefill chunk caps per-call m.
27b_leg: NOT re-run in this lane. v1's 27B pp leg was already uninformative for the kernel (the MEMRA_PP_FP8 stash duplicates F8-origin projections on top of the resident Q8_0, so a 3072 MB budget covered ~8.6 of 64 layers = 8.7% coverage, and it OOM'd at pp6257), and nothing in v2 changes the stash. The 27B claim in this lane is GEMM-only and labeled as such.

kernel_gate: fp8-mmq-check ALL GREEN at every geometry measured in this lane (slice 1, Y=64, OCC=2, PIPE=1, X=256, X=256+PIPE, final wave-fill rule): 9 shapes incl. ragged out_f, ragged in_f, mid-iteration k tail and m=1; EXACT arm 0 bit mismatches and 0 NaN; RAND arm rms_rel <= 1.5e-6; e4m3 code coverage 254/254 legal codes MEASURED, not asserted. The host reference was rewritten to v2's grouping — the reference defines the arithmetic and the gate proves the kernel implements it.
model_level: 99.5% dispatch coverage (25088/25216; the 128 refusals are the tied-embedding lm_head). Teacher-forced on the floor tape: 3/128 argmax disagreements, all near-ties (floor margins 0.023/0.128/0.172 against a median 3.6871, <= 0.047x median, within 1.22 sigma). 6-draw sampled: 2/192, both near-ties. NLL on the frozen held-out window: floor 1.280530 vs mmq 1.280540 = +0.0008% perplexity, against v1's +0.11% — ~130x closer to the floor DESPITE the 4x coarser activation scale, which is the e4m3-container argument (a coarser amax costs exponent headroom, not mantissa) holding up in practice.
geometry_invariance_receipt: the tf digest 0xb7bb29d7ce264198 and the 3/128 count reproduce EXACTLY across the pre-fix and post-fix selection rules. Different token tile, identical bits — the ARITHMETIC CONTRACT's claim, with evidence.

stop_rule_as_given: 'if after slices 1-3 the GEMM-only bench still can't reach 1.0x floor, the honest conclusion is that per-block FP8 has no prefill advantage on sm_120 — write that record, recommend killing MEMRA_FP8_MMQ, and conclude; do NOT spiral beyond the three recipe items plus at most 2 bounded experiments.'
which_branch: NEITHER cleanly, and the honest statement is the split one. GEMM-only DOES reach and pass 1.0x — but only on wide projections at large m, and only via the one geometry the restructure licensed, not via recipe items 2-3. It does not reach ~1.1x, and end-to-end on the local target model it is 0.99x. So: the kernel is no longer refuted (v1's 'not fast at any shape, any m, any tile' is now false), and it is also not shippable (a default flip needs >= 1.0x on the deployment model's own shapes, and 1.7B m=512 is 0.85-0.89x).
budget_spent: all 3 recipe items implemented and measured; exactly 2 bounded experiments (A: X=256 on the halved tile; B: X=256+PIPE to test slice 3's own mechanism note). No third experiment. The selection-rule fix is a bug fix found by the mandated pp leg, not a fourth variant — it changes which of two already-measured tiles runs.
recommendation: KEEP the arm, default OFF (MEMRA_FP8_MMQ=1), and do NOT flip any default. Do not kill the flag: v1's kill recommendation was predicated on 'slower at every shape', which v2 falsifies, and this is still the tree's only exact per-block-FP8 consumer. Per the flags doctrine the two CONCLUDED-NEGATIVE knobs SHOULD go: FP8_MMQ_PIPE (+ MEMRA_MMQ_PIPE_FP8) and the FP8_MMQ_OCC / MEMRA_MMQ_OCC_FP8 occupancy lever are refuted with receipts in RESULTS.jsonl and their dispatch arms are dead code. Left in place in this lane because deleting a build seam is an owner call and the rows are the record; flagged here as the one cleanup owed.
next_lever_if_anyone_resumes: not another tile sweep. The measured ceiling says the remaining gap is the f32 accumulator against the floor's s32, so the only untried structural move is to make the inner accumulation integer — quantize the e4m3 codes' mantissa field into an int8-compatible product per 128-block so the chain accumulates in s32 and the block scale still folds once. That is a different kernel with a different exactness contract (it would need its own host reference), not a v3 tuning pass, and it should not start without a receipted estimate that s32-vs-f32 accumulate is worth the >= 10pp it would have to buy.
